newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Real estate co, bank jump at debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Real estate co, bank jump at debut.

text.p: Shares of real estate manager LaSalle Partners Inc and a Little Rock, Arkansas bank jumped after their initial public offerings on Thursday.
LaSalle shares jumped 25 percent to close up 5/13 at 28-1/3, making it the top gaining stock on the New York Stock Exchange on a percent basis.

The jump in value came even though the initial price was much higher than first expected -- $23 a share -- well above its first estimated price range of $19 to $21 each. That range was ratcheted up to $21 to $23 because of high demand.
The Chicago company provides solutions for its clients' real estate needs such as management and financial services.
With four million shares sold, the IPO raised $92 million.

Shares of Bank of the Ozarks also jumped, up 2-3/8 from an IPO price of $16 a share, the top of price talk of $14 to $16. The bank holding company owns two state chartered subsidiary banks with a total of 11 branches and two loan production offices. According to its prospectus, its law firm is the Rose Law Firm of Little Rock.
